stories.title: Gold trades near one-year low as U.S. retail sales slow - Kitco AM Report
stories.description: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold was lower and spot silver was higher in early U.S. trading Tuesday, as investors assessed slowing U.S. consumer spending and persistent expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. Gold remained near its lowest level in more than a year, while silver recovered from Monday's selloff. Gold was trading near $3,845.26 an ounce, down $0.29%, while silver was trading near $47.428 an ounce, up 1.00%. The U.S. Commerce Department reported Tuesday that October retail and food services sales increased 0.2% to $748.2 billion, slowing from September's 0.8% increase and broadly matching economists' expectations. Sales were 6.8% higher than a year earlier, although the monthly increase was not statistically distinguishable from zero at the 90% confidence level. Sales excluding automobiles increased 0.6%, while sales excluding automobiles and gasoline advanced 0.5%. The figures indicate that consumer spending moderated following September's relatively strong performance, potentially easing some demand-driven inflation pressure. However, last week's stronger-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports, together with October's 165,000 increase in nonfarm payrolls, continue to support expectations for restrictive Federal Reserve monetary policy.Market positioning remains focused on the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting, with the latest published futures assessment indicating a 96.6% probability of a 25-basis-point increase and a 3.4% probability of a 50-basis-point move. The dollar eased modestly Tuesday after reaching its highest level since April 2025, while Treasury yields retreated from last week's elevated levels, providing limited support for gold. Investors will also assess October industrial production and capacity utilization, scheduled for 9:15 a.m. EST, followed by Wednesday's release of the minutes from the Fed's Oct. 27-28 meeting at 2 p.m. EST. The minutes could clarify policymakers' tolerance for persistent inflation and their assessment of labor-market risks. Softer economic activity or less hawkish commentary could reduce Treasury yields and support bullion, while continued inflation concerns would reinforce expectations for additional tightening.The Strait of Hormuz and U.S.-Iran situation remains a significant source of uncertainty for energy markets, although recovering Middle Eastern petroleum exports have reduced immediate supply concerns. Commercial shipping continues to face attacks and elevated security risks, but regional exporters have increased shipments toward prewar levels despite the unresolved confrontation. The International Energy Agency expects the global petroleum market to return to surplus during the fourth quarter as recovering supply outpaces demand growth. The U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and disagreements over sanctions, nuclear activities and maritime security remain unresolved, leaving the possibility of renewed disruption. For gold, continuing geopolitical uncertainty supports underlying defensive demand, although the potential inflationary consequences of another sustained oil-price increase could reinforce Fed tightening expectations.Crude oil prices were little changed Tuesday following Monday's decline of more than 3%, as expectations for a global supply surplus offset concerns about further attacks on tankers. Brent crude futures traded near $92.61 a barrel, up $0.17, or 0.18%, while Nymex WTI crude was near $85.73, up $0.01. Brent has declined approximately 22% so far in November, while WTI has fallen about 18%, reflecting the substantial reduction in the geopolitical risk premium as Middle Eastern exports recover. Lower energy prices could help moderate inflation expectations, although persistent underlying U.S. price pressure remains the more immediate consideration for Federal Reserve policy.Global equity markets remained under pressure before the U.S. open as concerns about artificial intelligence-related investment, restrictive monetary policy and corporate valuations continued to weigh on risk sentiment. Monday's U.S. session saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average decline approximately 1.4%, the S&P 500 lose 1.9% and the Nasdaq Composite fall 2.5%, led by renewed weakness in semiconductor and technology shares. Asian equities were generally weaker Tuesday, while European markets faced similar pressure from technology-sector selling and uncertainty surrounding interest rates. Investors remain particularly sensitive to corporate earnings and whether elevated financing costs will constrain artificial intelligence infrastructure investment.The key outside markets see Nymex WTI crude oil futures near $85.73 a barrel, while Brent crude was trading around $92.61. The U.S. dollar and Treasury yields were modestly lower after their recent advances, providing some relief for precious metals. However, expectations for another Federal Reserve rate increase in December continue to limit confidence in a sustained recovery. (Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.)Technically, spot gold bulls' next upside price objective is to push prices back above the $3,888.00 to $3,922.00 resistance zone, with a sustained move through the upper boundary needed to improve the near-term bearish technical outlook. Bears' next near-term downside price objective is a break below $3,832.00, with a deeper downside target at $3,805.00. First resistance is seen at $3,888.00 and then at $3,922.00. First support is seen at $3,832.00 and then at $3,805.00.Spot silver bulls' next upside price objective is to drive prices back above the $48.540 to $49.840 resistance zone, with a sustained move through the upper boundary needed to strengthen the recovery. The next downside price objective for the bears is a break below $46.920, with a deeper downside target at $45.580. First resistance is seen at $48.540 and then at $49.840. stories.title: Ternary choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents for continuous gas dehumidification: performance benchmarking against triethylene glycol
stories.description: This research evaluates deep eutectic solvents (DES) as potential alternatives to conventional glycol-based desiccants for gas dehydration, highlighting their low volatility, tunable composition, and strong water-binding abilities. However, experimental studies on novel ternary hygroscopic DESs designed for gas dehydration remain limited. In this study, we synthesized and tested a series of ternary choline chloride-based DESs for air moisture absorption and potential use in gas dehydration systems. We characterized their physical properties by measuring density, viscosity, and pH, and confirmed molecular interactions using FTIR and ¹H NMR spectroscopy. Air dehumidification experiments at room temperature with a controlled humidity system assessed the hygroscopic properties of these DESs. Water absorption rates and relative humidity were monitored throughout the tests. All six ternary DES formulations remained stable as single phases for 72 h. The ChCl: Lactic Acid: TEG and ChCl: Lactic Acid: MDEA systems achieved minimum relative humidity values of 1.3% and reduced the dew point temperature to − 35 °C. The ChCl: Acetamide: MeOH and ChCl: Citric Acid·H₂O: MeOH systems showed the highest water absorption capacities at 12.28 wt% and 12.39 wt%, respectively. These findings demonstrate a correlation between DES composition, physicochemical properties, and hygroscopic performance, highlighting the potential of these ternary DESs for dehumidification under the investigated laboratory conditions and their prospective application as liquid desiccants for natural-gas dehydration, subject to further validation under representative pressurized gas conditions.

stories.title: Associations of Epstein–Barr virus DNA and transcriptional activity with interferon signaling, pyroptosis, and microRNA signatures in oral lichen planus
stories.description: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory disorder, but the molecular factors shaping its immune response remain unclear. Here, we explored associations of Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) positivity with interferon, inflammasome, and microRNA expression in OLP. Public datasets lacked sample-level EBV status and informed OLP-associated pathway analysis and target prioritization. Separately, we examined oral tissues from 35 patients with OLP and 35 controls for EBV DNA; LMP1, BZLF1, and BRLF1 transcripts; genes involved in inflammation, interferon responses, and pyroptosis; and seven mature miRNAs. Transcriptomic analysis revealed consistent enrichment of interferon-γ, interferon-α, inflammatory response and TNF–NF-κB pathways in OLP. EBV DNA was detected in 8 of 35 OLP samples and 4 of 35 controls, although this difference was not significant. Among EBV-positive tissues, LMP1 was the most frequently detected viral transcript; the observed BZLF1 and BRLF1 differences were based on very few detectable specimens. OLP tissues displayed broad upregulation of genes involved in inflammation, interferon responses, and pyroptosis. The primary molecular signature was OLP-associated; after adjustment for disease status, no host marker retained a significant EBV association following correction for multiple testing. miR-155-5p, miR-146a-5p, miR-21-5p and miR-142-3p were increased in OLP, while miR-27b-3p was reduced. Overall, OLP was characterized by interferon and inflammatory responses, altered miRNAs, and transcriptional priming of pyroptosis-related pathways. EBV-associated findings are exploratory because the positive subgroups and transcript-detectable subsets were small, and pooled comparisons may be confounded by disease status. These data do not establish that EBV drives a distinct inflammatory program in OLP.

stories.description: Elementary particles and the forces governing their interactions are described by relativistic quantum field theory, in which symmetry serves as a fundamental guiding principle. For more than half a century, the possible symmetries of such theories were believed to be restricted by the Coleman–Mandula theorem and its supersymmetric extension, the Haag–Łopuszański–Sohnius theorem.

stories.title: Natural Cycles’ new wristband adds daytime activity tracking and a battery life boost.
stories.description:
The original NC Band launched earlier this year as an alternative to wearing an Apple Watch or Oura Ring overnight to collect temperature and activity data for the company’s controversial FDA-cleared birth control app. The new NC Band 2 boosts battery life to 21 days with a lighter and thinner design. It’s available for preorder today and comes free with a $149-per-year Natural Cycles subscription, while existing subscribers can get one for $99.
